note: Candidates from the 2026-08-15 verify pass on data/research/aarhus-candidates.json (Dansk Traeregister leads). 7 trees verified to data/research/aarhus-verified.json; the rest are here in the two kinds, leads and blocked.

leads.name: Asken i Grundfør
leads.why: Alive and genuinely remarkable: 5.52m girth, 23m tall, dendron.dk Individual_ID=1249 (GPS-verified 2019), rated nationally noteworthy and once recorded as Denmark's largest ash before being overtaken by a specimen at Kalo Hestehave. Independently corroborated by Kirker.dk as standing in Grundfor Praestegaardshave (the rectory/parsonage garden next to Grundfor Kirke). RE-CHECKED 2026-08-30: the access question actually resolves favourably, the former parsonage is now Hinnerup parish's shared church office (kirkekontor), open to the public Mon/Wed/Thu/Fri 09:00-12:30 per dinavis.dk and kirkenihinnerup.dk, so this is not a private home. What still blocks it is the day-trip boundary: Grundfor is a small hamlet roughly 3-4km beyond Hinnerup station (itself an 11-15 minute train ride from Aarhus centre), and no direct frequent bus link from Hinnerup to Grundfor could be confirmed, making the realistic door-to-door time very unlikely to land inside the ~30-minute public-transport day-trip boundary this project uses. Blocked on distance, not access; a future pass with a real Rejseplanen door-to-door time or a confirmed infrequent/school bus link could reopen this.

blocked.name: Blodbøgen på Randersvej
blocked.why: NEVER SHIP as an entry. Planted 1898 by gardener Jens Lassen Faurschou as a memorial to General Rye and the 1849 cavalry battle at Aarhus. FELLED in February 2011 to widen Randersvej for light rail; dendron.dk Individual_ID=508 itself records status 'Dod' (Dead), age given only 'ved faeldningen i 2010' (at the felling). About 30 cuttings were taken and clones planted elsewhere, including one in Vennelyst Park, so a living clone could be a future candidate under a different entry, but the original tree this candidate named is gone. Sources: dendron.dk detaljer.asp?Individual_ID=508, da.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blodboegen_paa_Randersvej, stiften.dk coverage of the felling and the clone replanting.

blocked.name: Niels Ebbesens Eg
blocked.why: NEVER SHIP as an entry. A legendary oak at Nørreris Voldsted, Hinnerup, said to have been planted by the father of the medieval hero Niels Ebbesen and long believed 500-600 years old. Fell in a storm in 1992 after root rot; dendron.dk Individual_ID=1757 itself records status 'Død' (Dead), legend 'Væltet 1992' (fell 1992). Also within the register under Individual_ID=179 and possibly others per the candidates file's note that this name appeared four times in the source KML. Sources: dendron.dk, hinneruparkiv.dk's own folder on the tree, ambirk.eu local history page.

blocked.name: Århusbøgene
blocked.blocked_reason: private land, not a collectible point
blocked.why: NEVER SHIP as an ordinary entry. A stand of old beeches on the slope between Niels W. Gades Vej and Strandvejen, protected since a 1928 ruling, but fredninger.dk's own page ('Aarhus, Bøgetræer') states plainly they form a boundary planting between private villa gardens ('en bevoksning af gamle bøge danner skel mellem villahaver'), visible from the two public streets but not on ground the public may enter. Also fails the collectible-point test on its own terms: it is a multi-tree boundary planting ('bevoksning'), not one identifiable tree or a compact ensemble with one obvious place to stand, closer to an avenue than a single collectible tree. Sources: dendron.dk Individual_ID=286 (also listed under WDPA site ID 333939), fredninger.dk/fredning/aarhus-boegetraeer/.
